About

Engineer by training. Product person by curiosity.

I’ve always liked taking things apart to see how they work. That curiosity led me to a mechanical engineering degree at Texas A&M, to R&D work with Japanese clients, and eventually to writing full-stack code for one of the world’s largest freelancing marketplaces. My days were all about the how: how to build it, how to make it fast, how to ship it cleanly.

But I kept asking why. Why does this feature matter to the business? Why would a client hire through us and not somewhere else? Which problem is worth solving first? I wanted to understand the strategy behind the work, not just carry it out, and that pulled me into product.

Today I lead a team delivering AI and automation projects. I start with the business problem, use data to decide what to build, and bring my engineering background to help the team build it well.

  • I speak engineer

    Years of writing full-stack code mean I can estimate realistically, weigh tech debt against features, and earn the trust of the engineers I work with.

  • I start with the why

    Before deciding what to build, I want to understand the business problem. I use user interviews and data to find the problem worth solving first.

  • I lead by serving

    I build light, collaborative teams where people feel safe to push back. I clear blockers, give actionable feedback, and protect the team’s focus.

Selected work

Problems I’ve shipped solutions for.

SPX Express · Senior Associate, Special Projects · 2026

AI image validation for fraud detection

Launched an AI tool that checks submitted images for fraud, so reviewers only see the cases that need a human.

  • 85% less manual fraud review volume
  • 50% less overall review time
  • AI
  • Automation
  • Operations

The problem

The operations team reviewed images for fraud by hand. As volume grew, manual review became a bottleneck in both cost and speed.

What I did

  • Scoped the problem into an AI-based validation tool that flags suspicious images and lets clean ones through.
  • Managed the launch end to end with my team of 4, from intake and prioritization through delivery.

The outcome

  • 85% less manual fraud review volume
  • 50% less overall review time

SPX Express · Senior Associate, Special Projects · 2026

KYC application processing automation

Automated the triage of KYC applications into Accept or Review, so reviewers spend their time on the cases that need judgment.

  • 46% less manual review time
  • Automation
  • Operations
  • KYC

The problem

Every KYC (Know Your Customer) application went through manual review, including the clear-cut ones.

What I did

  • Defined an automation that auto-classifies each submission as Accept or Review.
  • Worked with operations to agree on what makes a submission safe to accept automatically.

The outcome

  • 46% less manual review time

Freelancer.com · Associate Product Manager · 2023–2025

Client notification experiment

Used user interviews and A/B testing to change how clients are notified, which increased hired freelancers by 9%.

  • +9% hired freelancers
  • Marketplace
  • A/B testing
  • User research

The problem

In a two-sided marketplace, a freelancer only gets paid once a client hires them. Clients who posted a project weren’t always acting on it, so good freelancers lost work.

What I did

  • Revived the user interview process to understand freelancer and client workflows, and found friction points worth testing.
  • Designed and ran an iterative A/B test on client notifications.
  • Partnered with international engineering and design teams to ship each iteration.

The outcome

  • +9% increase in hired freelancers

Freelancer.com · Software Engineer · 2021–2023

Chat suggestions for freelancers

Built full-stack features as an engineer to test marketplace hypotheses, including chat suggestions that help freelancers win more work.

  • Engineering
  • Marketplace
  • A/B testing

The problem

Freelancers often lose a project in the first few messages with a client. Could we help them respond better and faster?

What I did

  • Built the full-stack feature behind an A/B test to validate the hypothesis.
  • Pushed a shift-left mindset with QA so edge cases were caught early instead of turning into scope creep.

The outcome

This is where I learned to think like a PM: start with the hypothesis, then build only enough to test it.

Advanced World Solutions · Assistant R&D Engineer · 2017–2020

Test case automation tool

Built a tool that automated test case creation from Japanese test scenarios for a major Japanese video game company, nearly doubling the team’s test creation speed.

  • ~2× faster test case creation
  • Automation
  • Engineering
  • Japanese clients

The problem

On a project for a major Japanese video game company, our team received test scenarios written in Japanese and had to turn each one into test cases by hand. It was slow, repetitive work, and the volume kept growing.

What I did

  • Built an automation tool that generated test cases from the scenarios, replacing most of the manual writing.

The outcome

  • Test case creation speed increased by almost 100%, nearly doubling the team’s output.
